solutions.title: One booking and patient system for all three branches
solutions.why: Paper bookings across three branches make it hard to see free chairs, patient history and the day's income in one place. A shared clinic system puts schedules, dental records and payments for every branch on one screen for the owner.
solutions.difficulty_reason: Three branches, several staff roles and moving paper records into the system.uh

solutions.title: Patients book a dentist themselves in Telegram
solutions.why: Today every booking goes through the phone and paper. A Telegram bot lets patients pick a branch, doctor and free slot themselves and get reminders, which cuts calls and missed visits.
solutions.difficulty_reason: Needs live free slots from the clinic system for each branch.

not_recommended.why: A Telegram bot covers patient booking for three branches without the cost of a separate app.
Moving bookings off paper and into self-booking should come before automating phone calls.

pick.roadmap_note: Start with the shared clinic system so all branches book in one calendar, then connect the Telegram booking bot to it.

Staff have computers or tablets at the reception desks.
Patient records are kept on paper and need to be moved in.

list.text: A restaurant with delivery, orders by phone and Telegram

heard.summary: A single restaurant with delivery takes orders by phone and Telegram and wants more sales.

questions.text: Should customers pay online when they order?
Do you use iiko or R-Keeper at the restaurant?

solutions.title: Telegram ordering bot with menu and delivery pin
solutions.why: Your customers already order through Telegram, so a bot with your menu lets them order without waiting for a staff reply and sends each order straight to your team. Fewer orders get lost in chat, and ordering becomes easier, which supports sales.
solutions.difficulty_reason: Standard bot; menu setup and delivery address handling need care

solutions.title: Cashback in Telegram to bring delivery customers back
solutions.why: Repeat orders are the cheapest way to grow sales for one restaurant. Cashback in the same Telegram channel gives customers a reason to order again.
solutions.difficulty_reason: Simple rules, but must link to orders from the bot

solutions.title: Phone line that records calls and shows missed ones
solutions.why: Phone orders still matter, and a missed call during a busy hour is a lost order. Calls go to a free person and missed calls are shown so someone calls back.
solutions.difficulty_reason: Needs a SIP number and setup on staff phones

not_recommended.why: A branded app is costly for one restaurant, and your customers already use Telegram.
Courier and dispatcher apps pay off with many couriers and branches, not one kitchen.

pick.roadmap_note: Start with the ordering bot, add cashback once orders flow through it, then improve the phone line if missed calls remain a problem.
pick.first_step: Put your current menu with prices, photos and delivery zones into one document so the bot can be filled.
assumptions: The restaurant runs its own couriers.
Most phone and Telegram orders are for delivery.
There is no existing website or online menu.

deliverables_mvp: Cloud phone line on your current number or a new short number
Voice greeting and menu in Uzbek and Russian

Simple call log showing who answered and when

AI voice agent to take orders at night

Number switched over, staff shown how to answer and call back

risks.mitigation: Start the number request in the plan phase or forward the old number meanwhile

risks.text: Staff ignore missed-call alerts during the rush
risks.mitigation: Name one person per shift responsible for call-backs

solutions.difficulty_reason: Simple bot, but the report form must fit how 15 drivers actually work on the road

solutions.title: GPS and fuel control for the 15 trucks
solutions.why: Paper reports cannot show where a truck really was or how much fuel it burned. GPS monitoring shows routes, idle time and fuel per driver, which is the control you are asking for.
solutions.difficulty_reason: Trackers must be fitted and checked on every vehicle, fuel sensors need calibration

not_recommended.why: A full transport management system is too much for one city base moving off paper; start with digital reports and grow later if needed.
Drivers already have Telegram, so a separate mobile app is not needed for reporting.

pick.roadmap_note: Start with the Telegram report bot so paper stops quickly, then add GPS monitoring and compare its data with the drivers' reports.
pick.first_step: Collect one week of current paper reports and list the fields drivers fill in, so the bot form can copy them.
assumptions: Drivers have smartphones with Telegram and mobile internet.
Trucks do not yet have GPS trackers.
Trips are planned by phone from one dispatcher.

deliverables_mvp: Telegram bot with a trip report form for drivers
Delivery photo with time and location check
All reports in one web table for the owner and dispatcher
Daily summary of trips per driver sent to the owner
Map links for each reported stop
Simple reports on trips and stops per driver
deliverables_full: Checklists with required photos for each delivery
Offline queue so reports send later when coverage drops
Map of all stops for the day
Performance figures per driver

phases.deliverable: Report form agreed with the owner and two or three drivers
Bot, photo and location checks, web table and daily summary
A week of real trips with a few drivers, form fixed after
All 15 drivers onboarded, paper reports stopped

risks.text: Some drivers keep using paper or skip reports because the bot feels like extra work
risks.mitigation: Keep the form to a few taps and have the owner make bot reports the only accepted way

risks.text: Phone location is off or turned off at some stops
risks.mitigation: Ask for location with each photo and flag reports that arrive without it

needs: A list of the 15 drivers with their Telegram accounts
The current paper report form and what each field means
A decision on who checks the reports each day
A person with authority to tell drivers paper reports end
Two or three drivers willing to test the bot first

impact.summary: The owner sees every trip during the day, and no one has to collect and retype paper reports.

inputs.label: How many hours a week go to collecting and checking paper reports?
What does one office hour of that work cost you, in USD?

deliverables_mvp: GPS trackers fitted or reused on all 15 trucks
Live map showing where every truck is now
Trip and stop history per truck and driver
Geofences around the base and key client sites
Fuel level sensors on the trucks that burn the most
Telegram alerts for fuel drops, long stops and leaving zones
deliverables_full: Driver behaviour scores for speeding and harsh driving
Maintenance schedules by mileage and engine hours
Planned against actual routes for each trip
Links to waybills and 1C
Driver app and reports per vehicle and driver

phases.deliverable: List of trucks, chosen trackers and fuel sensors, alert rules
Trackers and sensors fitted, live map and trip history running
Fuel sensors calibrated, routes checked against real trips
All 15 trucks on the map, owner and dispatcher get alerts

risks.text: Trucks are on the road all day, so fitting trackers takes longer than planned
risks.mitigation: Fit trackers at the base in the evening or on rest days, a few trucks at a time

risks.text: Fuel sensors give wrong readings on some tank shapes
risks.mitigation: Calibrate each tank with measured fills before trusting the numbers

risks.text: Drivers resist being tracked or tamper with devices
risks.mitigation: Explain the rules up front and alert on power loss from any tracker

needs: List of all 15 trucks with plate, model and tank size
Time slots when each truck can stand at the base for fitting
Budget decision on trackers and fuel sensors, quoted separately
Addresses of the base and regular client sites for geofences
A dispatcher or manager who receives and acts on alerts
Telegram accounts for the owner and that manager

impact.summary: The owner sees real routes, stops and fuel use instead of paper reports, so fuel theft and unrecorded trips become visible and drop.

inputs.label: How many fuel losses or unexplained trips happen in a month across the fleet?
What share of these losses would tracking stop?
What does one fuel loss or unrecorded trip cost you, in USD?
